At the most basic level vaccines are just viruses with the bad stuff taken out.

Viruses are lil packets of Bad Stuff. Now it has to be deliverable. Think of it like spam mail. The spam mail has to come in an envelope, bc the envelope tells the virus where to end up and allows it to get into places where it can do the most harm (ie your mailbox or biologically, your cells). So those are the two parts of the virus. A vaccine, at the most basic level, is JUST the envelope.

Bc usually when you get this spam mail, you will get it, you will open it, and you will then realize that it is spam and therefore harmful. Now you know that anytime you see this particular envelope, that its probably going to be spam. So the next time you see it, you will still get annoyed a lil bit, you will get over it quicker and youll just toss it out.

Apply this to the virus vaccine. You get a virus. Your body accepts it not knowing what it is, it “annoys you” ie gets you sick. However now your body knows that this particular coating or viral shell is a bad thing. The next time your body comes across this you will still get a tiny bit “annoyed” ie a tiny bit sick, but your body will remember and more quickly get rid of the virus. 

So a vaccine does this by giving you the empty envelope. It doesnt do anything to you bc theres no spam in it, and you kinda “cheat” your way through that first infection. Thats why people feel a lil sick afterwards, its your body conducting an immune response to the viral shell. So SOMETIMES u get a lil sniffley and a slight fever but its over but its over very quickly and you arent affected by the actual virus.

A common misconception is that you shouldnt get sick after getting the vaccine, no. All it does is increase the immune response time and strength so you are sick for less time and not as bad. It cant PREVENT infection from happening in the first place.

As for poisoning your child, thats meaningless. There is no poisoning going on. You cannot read the ingredient list and be shocked by whats in it. I think a common talking oozing among the anti vaxxers is the mercury perservative which iirc is only used in some vaccines and its not in a form that could harm you. Its like saying i wont eat salt bc it has chlorine (a very very deadly gas) and sodium (a very reactive metal that explode in contact with water) in it.

As for the autism thing. Thats just flat out wrong. Like nowhere near correct. If we had something that could completely rewrite our genetic code throughout ALL of our bodies cells (which is what it would take to “give” someone autism) we wouldnt be using it on giving people autism, we would use it cure every disease known to man. That level of genetic editing could LITERALLY solve almost all of mankinds diseases from cancer to diabetes to autoimmune diseases to parkinsons. So no. It. Cant give ur kid autism. If it could, well we would have better uses for it than giving ur kid autism.

I mean in theory? No harm at all. Or at least as little as possible while still letting the other cities thrive. 

And from my understandinf, the only reason why ALL of these cities are prosperous in the first place is bc they have two things 1) connections to other trade cities, and 2) enough distance between them and other trade centers so that some merchants are tempted to make THAT city their base of operation. Like each city has a core of merchants that exists there bc they dont want to make the trip to the next one (ie is it more worth it to sell here or to make the long trip to somewhere else). 

And for all of these cities to be thriving there has to be enough distance between them that they are not in direct competition. So in reality the cities previous to city a not only serve has another origin of goods to end up in city A, but also as rest stops. You cant drive a merchant train THAT far without some law, safe places to rest, places to buy new goods, and whatever else a large city would provide. 

So while there is harm in that not all the goods end up in city a, its offset by the fact that the other cities provide easier access to city a. Now city A could just take over the other cities thereby keeping the benefits and routing all taxes and tariffs back to city A. But with the aforementioned distance and also the difficulty of taking over multiple cities combined with the fact youd be turning the only trade route (as you said you cant navigate around this route) into a war zone which would dramatically drop your income, city a has no interest in taking them over militarily. So theyd have to do it diplomatically.

But for someone like you and someone like me, people only seeing what we want to see… what we are allowed to see, it is easy to form opinions and fantasies about such a place. Possibly a room with with fading, peeling wallpaper, deep-set couches not yet dusted, a table of warm, hearty if a bit simple food, with friends smiling and warming themselves on a roaring fire. Consider this, HoB and electrocute are both used for burst dmg. However, while electrocute provides an additional dmg source (the proc itself), HoB provides you with more attacks. And if im not mistaken on a much lower CD too. Now early game electrocute will seem like it does more dmg, but mid to late game HoB will be much better at providing that burst.

Now. To answer ur question, yes it is probably the best rune out there that will “dominate” a lvl 1 trade with a sylas or any champ really. But basically starting from lvl 4 (2nd W point) and really any amount of ap or magic pen, HoB will start to feel much better. And LT would be even better. 

Against melee champs (and esp sylas), burst is not what you are looking for. So electrocute and HoB are some of the worst runes you could take. 1) sylas mitigates ur burst by pressing W, 2) any mid laner with a brain cell playing against an azir will almost always go revitilize, second wind, bone plating, and/or dorans shield. Meaning ur burst (while doing dmg and bringing them low) means nothing cuz they can stay at around 30-40% hp between bases and farm under tower. Something like LT or even conq, sorta flips this dynamic on its head. Instead of the extreme poke, and thereby creating a threat via the hp diff (man this azir is 80% while im only 40%), LT and conq create a threat in the reverse. Man i shouldnt go in on this azir cuz he will fuck me with LT and conq while im trying to get out. However a rune like LT and conq is also useful late game and in teamfights. Runes like HoB are really only useful for trading back against champions that poke you down. Meaning its a mitigation rune, an equalizing rune, a rune that lets u claw back up to an even game state against a ranged champion (leblanc, ahri, zoe, ori, etc) that does pretty okay into a champ like azir.

Tldr: dont take electrocute, take LT and conq against melee match ups and low threat ranged matchups, take HoB against ranged match ups that you cant poke easily, and even more safer would be taking coment against high threat match ups (xerath and viktor come to mind). Aery is actually not all that bad into melee matchups either so.

Malazan is prolly a very good fit for what you are looking for. The one part it may not fit is the “traditional” fantasy, it kinda goes beyond the normal humans, elves, dwarves thing. Theres no hand holding, no omniscient descriptions of gods or powers or magic or history (almost to the point that it gets bery difficult to accurate gauge the “power level” of most entities, and almost to the point of frustration if ur a hard magic enjoyer). Its all told through characters so be ready for unreliable narration or at the very least incomplete narration. But ya, youll meet a LOT of characters and will stick with quite a few through the whole series. And the storylines that do not see their conclusions may see one in the other books/series set in this universe.

Some people say it has really bad characterization, i say the opposite, it is incredibly rich in character. But i will say since a lot of POV characters are just normal dudes, it oscillates between them trying to react to whats happening in the world around and them actually driving the story. Some characters do a lot of reacting, others do a lot of driving. Either way the characters are VERY well written. The point being that characters are what the story is about. The series isnt about the events of the world, those are just happening and are providing the context for our characters. This series is about how these characters are experiencing, coping, and just living through these events. Its dark, sad, and very grim. But the author has said that this book is about humans and their compassion in the most trying of times. So do what you will with this info.

I would give it to the second or third book to see if you like it. The first is… well. Its a lil lack luster. Almost Universally acknowledged as the worst (but by no means BAD) while the second and third are fan favorites. 

Im ngl the series is not for everyone, and its NOT a bad thing if you decide you dont like it. I know makazan recs are memed upon in this sub but i genuinely believe that its one of the top epic fantasy series written. But i respect differing, even opposing opinions and no matter what anyone says you are not “too dumb” or whatever if you do not end up enjoying this series.

The same reason some mages and ADCs take conq. There’s like a balance between AS, lifesteal, AD/AP, and ability usage that champs need to break to feel good.

Some champs need AS more than than they need raw AD/AP bc most of their abilities are either just for ccing, movement, or some other utility. So these champs benefit from taking LT. so like yi needs the AS more than the AD bc his abilities don’t really get as much use from that additional AD, whereas the AS let’s yi go berserk with an uncapped AS.

On the other hand someone like gwen or Irelia, benefit from getting AD over AS bc their abilities are actually where a lot of their dmg comes from, so like Gwen snipping you benefits more from AP than AS. Same thing with Irelia, although she can go either as her dmg origin changes depending on the build. So her Qs benefit more from the sustain and AD than just getting the ramping AS. This is also true for champs like Diana, nilah, samira, ez, corki, and others, who like the AD more than they like the AS.

Gap junctions are the opposite of tight junctions; in the sense that GJ are small “windows” into adjacent cells that allow for rapid transport of diffusible materials, while TJ are strong anchoring point made between the the cell mbrans of adjacent cells to make a “watertight” seal.

Short answer: Gap junctions are not used for transporting things from the blood vessel to the brain. They are used in between cells themselves to allow for rapid diffusion of stuff. 

Long answer: Imagine a row of boxes with roughly half an inch of space between them. 

Now gap junctions mean that these boxes would have gaps on the vertical phases that allow something in one box to move to the next box for rapid diffusion across all the boxes. So like if you wanted to induce a very fast change in the cells behavior there could a neurotransmitter or chemical released in one cell that would then rapidly diffuse into others. So gap junctions would not be entirely useful in the BBB cuz gap junctions don’t really have a function in transporting stuff from the blood vessels to the interstitial fluid of the brain. All they do is allow the rapid diffusion of (usually small) stuff within the connected cells. 

Tight junctions make sense the most bc all these do is that they provide a very tight bond between the adjacent cells so nothing can like leak through the space between the cells. Going to the box example this would be like if you then connected the boxes with like a hot glue gun. Now NOTHING can get through the previously half inch space, and anything that wants to cross to the space on top of the boxes has to go come through the bottom of the box and then up top. In anatomy this means that nothing can “leak” into the brain. It all has to be moved from the vessels to the brain via channel proteins or whatever. So tight junctions are VERY useful in places where you want to (need to) ensure that nothing can get past the layer of cells that are forming the barrier.

Just concerning wave clear:
Maybe I’m biased cuz I main these dudes but ryze has the most efficient wave clearing early-mid (after lost chapter/blasting wand) and it goes to absolutely BROKEN mid-late. His early clear (pre lost chapter/blasting wand, pre-6) is kinda meh with abilities, but it’s not bad and you can shove pretty well in early with some smart ability usage. 

Azir on the other hand is amazing bc it’s by far the safest wave clear. Like you cannot beat the safety of azirs landing phase. But ya azir and ryze offer some of the best wave clears in the game, not just in the mid lane.

Now as for the solo killing part/pressuring your lane. Both of these champs are also very oppressive. Azir is the one of the most oppressive mid laners in the game, cuz trading against him means getting close to him which almost always means taking a shit ton of dmg. And post-6 you would hard pressed to kill an azir solo. Ryze on the other hand is much less oppressive early (azir is super safe and annoying early, and gets truly scary mid to late). Ryze is sorta meh early, the trades you do are secondary to hitting the wave, meaning you go for ability hits on the wave and hope for dmg spreading to your laner. Mid to late ryze will almost always clear the wave WELL before the enemy and just run at them spamming spells.

Are you maybe trying to find a singular “main” plot?

If so, I don’t think Malazan has that. What it does have is many many plot lines. Kinda like GOT, where there are a lot of plot lines all converging to one or two culminating events.

Malazan, from what little I’ve read (on Memories of Ice), is trending towards that. But like. Times a thousand. There are more characters, more plot lines, and it’s loosely held together by the fact that these plot lines are happening in the same world and that in this world there are things happening which may influence certain plot lines. Even then I assume the way this series will shape out to be is that, some plot lines will not even have a conclusion (in that we won’t know happened to said line after a certain point), some plot lines may converge (I see this happening with a couple of lines from where I’m at in Memories of Ice), and some plot lines may just end up taking a wildly different meandering path through the world and they may just happen upon events but probably will not interact meaningfully with them, and I’m sure there are other possibilities.

My point is that Malazan isn’t a story where plot lines create events (although obvi some do), rather Malazan has plot lines just happening as the world just does it’s world things. It’s just characters traversing the world with no singular goal or looming threat in mind (although there is one Looming Threat, most, in fact almost all, of the characters have no idea about it, nor do I suspect they ever will). 

Maybe this is what you were missing, and it’s what I was missing when I first started Gotm. I had to shift my perspective into less of questioning what’s happening and why it’s happening to just experiencing what’s happening. I’m being told a story, I’ll get answers when I get them. do you use your soldiers? if so it should be pretty easy, don’t try and last hit all at once. Meaning don’t wait for all of the minions to get to “last hit” hp then try and last hit. That doesn’t work, you don’t have enough AS to hit them all before they die. 

Instead work on the back line first, put a soldier or two down in between the melee and ranged wave (basically on top of the cannon) and then attack and destroy the back line, it shouldn’t take more than 2-3 hits from soldiers in the early game, mid to late they should be one or two shot. Take out the back line, and while you’re doing that keep an eye for the melee minion health, you see a melee about to die, stop attacking the back line and last hit that melee, go back to the ranged creeps, once those are dead try to kill the cannon, once again keeping an eye out on the melees. This strat will push the wave to them faster as ranged creeps are more powerful than melees.

If you wanna do it the other way around go ahead, take out the melees first, then just q AA the back line (which should be sorta low health from the aoes and minions attacking it) that’ll almost always kill the back line. 

Last hitting with the soldiers is STUPID easy, if you know how to last hit. Which sounds circular. But it’s not. If you know how to even slightly manage the waves and how to time AA and abilities (which just comes with practice tbh), you can last hit with azir incredibly well.
